He played [[college basketball]] for [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]]. ==High school career== [[File:20160330 MCDAAG Sacha Killeya-Jones inbounds.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Killeya-Jones at the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2016 McDonald's All-American Game]]]] Killeya-Jones grew up playing [[American football|football]] at the [[quarterback]] position. As a freshman at [[Woodberry Forest School]] in Woodberry Forest, Virginia, he played football, a year before giving up the sport in exchange for basketball, which better suited his height and build.{{cite web |last1=Cates |first1=Ben |title=2016 All-Area Boys Basketball |url=https://www.newsadvance.com/sports/high_school/all-area-boys-basketball/article_e2622470-0f43-11e6-833e-63cfc6fc64a4.html |website=[[The News & Advance]] |accessdate=March 21, 2020 |date=May 1, 2016}} For his final two years, Killeya-Jones transferred to [[Virginia Episcopal School]] in [[Lynchburg, Virginia]]. In his senior season, he averaged 23.6 points, 10 rebounds and three blocks per game and led his team to a VISAA Division II state title.{{cite web |last1=Brown |first1=CL |title=Out of the Kentucky glare, Sacha Killeya-Jones finds peace with the Wolfpack |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/520687/2018/09/14/out-of-the-kentucky-glare-sacha-killeya-jones-finds-peace-with-the-wolfpack/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=March 21, 2020 |date=September 14, 2018}} He was also selected to play in the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2016 McDonald's All-American Game]].{{cite web |last1=Cates |first1=Ben |title=Sacha Killeya-Jones follows Staples' footsteps into McDonald's All-American Game |url=https://www.newsadvance.com/sports/high_school/sacha-killeya-jones-follows-staples-footsteps-into-mcdonald-s-all/article_ddcfa885-d7ed-538e-a0c5-909481b7dac6.html |website=[[The News & Advance]] |accessdate=March 21, 2020 |date=January 22, 2016}} Killeya-Jones left high school as a consensus five-star [[college recruit|recruit]]. He originally committed to [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] before switching to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]].{{cite magazine |last1=Johnson |first1=Chris |title=2016 four-star PF Sacha Killeya-Jones commits to Kentucky |url=https://www.si.com/college/2015/08/19/kentucky-lands-four-star-pf-sacha-killeya-jones |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |accessdate=March 21, 2020 |date=August 19, 2015}} ==College career== As a freshman at [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], Killeya-Jones played 14 games, averaging 2.9 points and 2.2 rebounds in 6.9 minutes per game. He did not play for much of the second half of the season, logging minutes in 14 total games.{{cite web |last1=Oakes |first1=Zac |title=Sacha Killeya-Jones gets high praise from Derek Willis |url=https://www.aseaofblue.com/2017/4/27/15441746/sacha-killeya-jones-high-praise-derek-willis |publisher=A Sea Of Blue |accessdate=March 22, 2020 |date=April 27, 2017}} In his sophomore season, he became a more frequent contributor off the bench, averaging 3.3 points and 2.9 rebounds in 13.7 minutes per game through 34 appearances.{{cite web |last1=Upchurch |first1=Matt |title=Sacha Killeya-Jones Transfer: An unfortunate Kentucky basketball casualty |url=https://wildcatbluenation.com/2018/04/12/sacha-killeya-jones-transfer-unfortunate-kentucky-casualty/ |publisher=Wildcat Blue Nation |accessdate=March 22, 2020 |date=April 12, 2018}} After the season, Killeya-Jones announced that he was transferring from Kentucky.{{cite web |last1=Boone |first1=Kyle |title=Former five-star recruit Sacha Killeya-Jones announces he's transferring from Kentucky |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/former-five-star-recruit-sacha-killeya-jones-announces-hes-transferring-from-kentucky/ |work=[[CBS Sports]] |accessdate=March 22, 2020 |date=April 9, 2018}} On May 15, 2018, he committed to continue his career at [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]] and sit out his next season due to [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) transfer rules.{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Sacha Killeya-Jones transferring to NC State from Kentucky |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/23513353/sacha-killeya-jones-kentucky-wildcats-transfer-nc-state-wolfpack |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=March 22, 2020 |date=May 15, 2018}} On February 28, 2019, before becoming eligible to play, Killeya-Jones left NC State to pursue a professional career.{{cite web |last1=Giglio |first1=Joe |title=Sacha Killeya-Jones leaves NC State to pursue pro career |url=https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/nc-state/article226960114.html |website=[[The News & Observer]] |accessdate=March 22, 2020 |date=February 28, 2019}} ==Professional career== ===2019–22=== In April 2019, Killeya-Jones joined Get Better Academy, a private basketball academy based in [[Prague]].{{cite web |last1=Roush |first1=Nick |title=Sacha Killeya-Jones lands in the Czech Republic |url=https://kentuckysportsradio.com/basketball-2/sacha-killeya-jones-lands-in-the-czech-republic/ |publisher=Kentucky Sports Radio |accessdate=March 22, 2020 |date=April 16, 2019}} He played 12 games for the academy team [[BC Sparta Praha|Sparta Praha]] of the 1.Liga, the second-tier Czech basketball league, and averaged 18.7 points and 8.3 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=Michael Finke and Sacha Killeya-Jones are Kalev players |url=https://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/michael-finke-and-sacha-killeya-jones-are-kalev-players/ |publisher=[[VTB United League]] |accessdate=March 22, 2020}} On July 11, Killeya-Jones signed with [[Basketball Löwen Braunschweig|Braunschweig]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]], the top-tier German league, but never played an official game with the team due to injury.{{cite web |title=Löwen verpflichten vielseitigen Big Man Sacha Killeya-Jones |url=https://www.basketball-loewen.de/presse/news/einzelner-beitrag/article/loewen-verpflichten-vielseitigen-big-man-sacha-killeya-jones.html |publisher=[[Basketball Löwen Braunschweig]] |accessdate=March 22, 2020 |language=German |date=July 11, 2019 |archive-date=22 March 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200322155034/https://www.basketball-loewen.de/presse/news/einzelner-beitrag/article/loewen-verpflichten-vielseitigen-big-man-sacha-killeya-jones.html |url-status=dead }} For the 2019–20 season, he signed with [[BC Kalev|Kalev/Cramo]], an Estonian team competing in the [[Latvian-Estonian Basketball League]] and [[VTB United League]]. He averaged 10.3 points and 4.0 rebounds per game for the club.{{cite news |last1=Varney |first1=Dennis |title=Catch up with 36 ex-Cats playing pro basketball in leagues outside the NBA |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/ex-cats/article241420196.html |accessdate=May 16, 2020 |work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |date=March 26, 2020}} On July 13, 2020, Killeya-Jones signed with [[MKS Dąbrowa Górnicza (basketball)|MKS Dąbrowa Górnicza]] of the [[Polish Basketball League]].{{cite news |last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano |title=Sacha Killeya-Jones inks with MKS Dabrowa Gornicza |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/sacha-killeya-jones-inks-with-mks-dabrowa-gornicza/ |newspaper=Sportando |accessdate=July 13, 2020 |date=July 13, 2020}} He averaged 19 points, 8.9 rebounds, 2 assists and 2 blocks per game, but left the team in January 2021 after suffering a torn Patellar Tendon. On August 23, 2021, Killeya-Jones signed with [[Hapoel Gilboa Galil]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{cite web |title=Sacha Killeya-Jones (ex MKS DG) joins H.Galil Gilboa |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Israel/news/701492/Sacha-Killeya-Jones-(ex-MKS-DG)-joins-H.Galil-Gilboa |website=Eurobasket |access-date=August 23, 2021 |date=August 23, 2021}} In 2021–22, he led the league in scoring, averaging 18.4 points per game.{{Cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/league/11/Israeli-BSL/stats/2022/Averages/Qualified/All/points/All/desc/1/Regular_Season|title=Israeli BSL Stats - RealGM|website=basketball.realgm.com}} ===Oklahoma City Blue (2022–2023)=== On October 2, 2022, Killeya-Jones signed with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] as [[Sterling Brown (basketball)|Sterling Brown]] was waived.{{cite magazine|first=Derek|last=Parker|title=Thunder Sign Sacha Killeya-Jones, Waive Sterling Brown|url= https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/.amp/news/thunder-sign-sacha-killeya-jones-waive-sterling-brown|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=October 2, 2022|access-date=October 3, 2022}} In his first preseason game with the Thunder, he recorded one block against [[Vlatko Čančar]]. After just one preseason game, he was waived on October 4. On November 3, he was named to the opening night roster for the [[Oklahoma City Blue]].{{cite web|title=Oklahoma City Blue Roster 2022-23|url=https://oklahomacity.gleague.nba.com/roster|website=NBA.com|date=November 3, 2022|access-date=November 3, 2022}} ===Surne Bilbao Basket (2023–present)=== On June 30, 2023, Killeya-Jones signed with [[Bilbao Basket|Surne Bilbao Basket]] of the [[Liga ACB]].{{cite web|title=Sacha Killeya-Jones se convierte en hombre de negro|url=https://bilbaobasket.biz/sacha-killeya-jones-se-convierte-en-hombre-de-negro/|website=BilbaoBasket.biz|date=June 30, 2023|access-date=July 2, 2023|language=Spanish}} ==National team career== Killeya-Jones, who has a British-born mother, is a [[multiple citizenship|dual citizen]] of the United States and the [[United Kingdom]]. He represents [[Great Britain national basketball team|Great Britain]] at the international level. Killeya-Jones attended the team's training camp for [[EuroBasket 2017|FIBA EuroBasket 2017]].{{cite web |last1=Page |first1=Fletcher |title=Kentucky's Sacha Killeya-Jones to attend Great Britain national team training camp |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2017/07/21/uk-basketball-uks-killeya-jones-attend-great-britain-tryout/501138001/ |website=[[The Courier-Journal]] |accessdate=March 22, 2020 |date=July 21, 2017}} He earned his first international cap against Ukraine in the Patras Tournament on 7 August 2017, but did not play, he was only 18-years-old. A few days later, Killeya-Jones saw action for the first time and scored 9 points vs Israel in a closed international test match. He played for Great Britain at [[EuroBasket 2021 qualification|FIBA EuroBasket 2022 qualifiers]].{{cite web |last1=Gains |first1=Bradley |title=GB Senior Men's final 12 confirmed for EuroBasket qualifiers |url=https://www.hoopsfix.com/2020/02/gb-senior-mens-final-12-confirmed-for-eurobasket-qualifiers-2/ |publisher=Hoopsfix |accessdate=March 22, 2020 |date=February 21, 2020}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://ukathletics.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/sacha-killeya-jones/4123 Kentucky Wildcats bio] {{Israeli Basketball Premier League Top Scorers}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Killeya-Jones, Sacha}} [[Category:1998 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:21st-century British sportsmen]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in the Czech Republic]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Estonia]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Israel]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Japan]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Poland]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Spain]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Middlesex County, New Jersey]] [[Category:BC Kalev/Cramo players]] [[Category:British men's basketball players]] [[Category:Hapoel Gilboa Galil players]] [[Category:Kawasaki Brave Thunders players]] [[Category:Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Oklahoma City Blue players]] [[Category:People from Highland Park, New Jersey]] [[Category:Power forwards]] [[Category:Virginia Episcopal School alumni]] [[Category:Woodberry Forest School alumni]]
